instruction: Save the blog article currently displayed in Chrome as a PDF file to /home/user/Documents/.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to download 2 blog articles as PDFs to /home/user/Documents/Blog. Successfully created the Blog directory, used Ctrl+P print dialog, navigated save dialogs, saved both PDFs, and switched between Chrome tabs. Failed because PDF filenames included Chrome's default suffix.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can use Ctrl+P to open print dialog, select 'Save as PDF', navigate file save dialog to specific directories, save PDF files, switch Chrome tabs
metadata.failure_analysis: Model saved PDFs with Chrome's default title format including ' _ Lil'Log' suffix. The evaluator script expected specific filenames. Model did not rename files.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified original task to saving just one page as PDF to a simpler location (/home/user/Documents/ instead of a subdirectory). Removes the complexity of renaming files and handling multiple tabs. The model demonstrated PDF saving capability in the trajectory.
metadata.explanation: Task requires saving the active blog page as PDF to /home/user/Documents/. Evaluator uses vm_command_line to count PDF files in Documents directory and check_file_count_gte custom metric to verify at least 1 PDF exists.

scoring_breakdown.pdf_saved: 1.0 - At least one PDF file exists in /home/user/Documents/

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly uses vm_command_line to count PDF files in /home/user/Documents/ with appropriate find command
Metric function correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' - directly accesses expected.get('min_count', 1) without wrapping in 'rules' key
Data flow is sound: command output (count string) -> int parsing -> comparison with min_count threshold
Evaluator verifies the core requirement: at least one PDF file saved to the correct directory
Minor limitation: does not verify PDF content is actually the blog article (could be any PDF), but this is a practical and reasonable simplification
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding a secondary check that the PDF filename contains keywords from the blog article title to verify correct content was saved
Could check PDF file size > 0 to ensure it's not an empty/corrupt file
